---
title: "Expected and realized errors among stated directions"
subtitle: "2.8 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), slides 22 and 25–26"
description: "Expected error shares, realized wrong counts and the joint probability that all statements are correct."
---

A report stating $N > 0$ directions has expected wrong share $E/N$; when $N = 0$, the share is undefined. Joint draws show how realized wrong counts and the all-right probability vary around $E$.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Start without draws.** States 14 of 15 pairs; expected share wrong is .0255 ($E \leq \tau N$ guaranteed).
- **Best report, draws.** Over 100 draws, mean wrong count is .360 (share .0257) vs. $E = .358$.
- **All withheld.** Every share reads “NA: no disclosure,” with vacuous all-right probability 1.
- **Three-unit law.** Expected share is 7/40 (B above C error 1/4, draw share 1/2); all-right is 3/4 (union bound 13/20).
- **Another coupling.** Pair errors and 7/40 stay fixed while exact all-right probability meets 13/20.

<details>
<summary>Optimality badge and joint-law notes</summary>

The badge “$E \leq \tau N$ applies” appears only for an exact optimum of the shown family when that family includes the all-withheld report; for any other report the badge states only whether $E \leq \tau N$ holds ($R \leq \tau$). Six-site draws sample independent normal latent values (Monte Carlo all-right estimates), whereas the three-unit law gives exact joint probabilities and union lower bounds (postrank theory book, chapters 10 and 15). Same-seed draws score any alternative report on the identical latent realizations.

</details>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
ev <- postrank_evaluate(c(A=1,B=2,C=3,D=3,E=4,F=5), pr_tutorial$one, weights=c(score_A=1), tau=.2)
ev[c("N", "E", "E_over_N")]
```
:::
